meta.title: Accessibility Statement — NexusFi
meta.description: NexusFi's commitment to digital accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), what has been done, what is in progress and how to report a barrier.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: NexusFi is working to make its platform — the public site and the logged-in area — usable by anyone, including people who use a screen reader, navigate by keyboard only, or rely on other assistive technologies. This follows the spirit of the Brazilian Inclusion Act (Law No. 13.146/2015), which treats digital accessibility as part of the right to access information and communication.

standard.title: The standard we follow
standard.body: Our technical reference is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, level AA — the most widely used international standard for web accessibility and the basis for eMAG (the Brazilian e-Government accessibility model) and ABNT NBR 17225 in Brazil.

done.title: What has been done
done.intro: This work was delivered in phases, covering the public site (landing page, sign-up, login, privacy policy) and the entire logged-in area (dashboard, cash flow, payables/receivables, cost centers, inventory, sales dashboard, taxes, reports and settings):
items: Full keyboard navigation for tables, cards, menus and filters that previously responded only to the mouse, with a visible focus indicator across the whole platform.

Windows and dialogs (modals) — including the four main entry modals (payables, receivables, taxes and cost centers) — announce their role and title to screen readers, trap focus while open and return focus exactly to whoever opened them on close, including closing with the Esc key.

Every icon-only button (close, edit, delete, navigate between photos, toggle theme, account menu, etc.) has an accessible name — more than 30 fixed during the audit — and dropdown menus report whether they are open or closed.
Sign-up, login and financial-screen forms with labels correctly tied to their fields (including option groups, using fieldset/legend).
A “Skip to content” link, visible on keyboard navigation, to skip the menu repeated on every page, with focus actually moving to the content (not just scrolling the page).
Heading order (H1 → H2 → H3) fixed on pages where a level was skipped, without changing the visual appearance.
The two hand-drawn financial charts on the dashboard have a table alternative (visually hidden, available to screen readers) with the same month-by-month values.
Reduced motion controlled by you — not by the operating system — under Settings → Appearance, with a “Reduced” option that removes transitions and turns off smooth scrolling.
A compact cookie notice, with an option to expand and see all categories before deciding.

Color contrast verified with real measurement (not just visual inspection) on all text of the reviewed screens, including the color tokens shared across the whole platform — two insufficient-contrast issues found in that measurement have already been fixed.

An automated check (lint with eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y) that now blocks, before going live, the types of accessibility problem found in this audit — today covering most of the logged-in-area pages, with the rest of the repository being added gradually.

limitations.title: Known limitations
items: PDF-exported reports have not been audited yet.

Two secondary modals (editing a cost center within Cost Centers, and the auxiliary Inventory modals) do not yet have the same complete accessible-dialog treatment as the four main modals — they remain usable by mouse and keyboard, but are not as screen-reader-ready.
The screen-reader test was done by inspecting the accessibility tree and the ARIA attributes, not with a real screen reader (NVDA/Narrator) running end to end.
Some pages outside the scope of this round (Users, developer area, subscription, design system) have not been audited yet.

report.title: How to report a barrier
report.body: If you find something on NexusFi that you couldn't use because of an accessibility barrier, write to us at <mail>{email}</mail>, describing the page, what you were trying to do and, if possible, the assistive technology you used. We'll review it and get back to you.
